title: Why the spinning Earth gives us day and night
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why do we have day and night?
Where does the Sun go at night?
How long does the Earth take to spin once?

stages.label: Night

explain.say: The Earth is a ball that spins like a top, making one full turn about every 24 hours. Only the half facing the Sun is lit, so as you turn into the light, the Sun appears to rise.

faq.q: Why does the Sun seem to rise?
faq.a: The Sun doesn't really move up. The Earth spins and carries you round until your side turns towards the Sun, so it appears over the eastern horizon.

faq.q: Where does the Sun go at night?
faq.a: Nowhere: it is still shining. Your side of the Earth has turned away from it, so the Sun is lighting up the other side of the planet, where it is daytime.
asks: Is the Sun still shining at night?

faq.q: How long does the Earth take to spin?
faq.a: About 24 hours to turn once relative to the Sun, which is one day. Measured against the distant stars, one spin takes 23 hours 56 minutes.

faq.q: Is it day and night at the same time on Earth?
faq.a: Yes. At any moment, half of the Earth is in daylight and half is in night. When it is midday in London, it is night in New Zealand.
asks: Is it night in Australia when it's day here?

faq.q: Why do we have time zones?
faq.a: Because midday arrives at different times around the world as the Earth turns. Countries set their clocks so that noon roughly matches when the Sun is highest, which gives the world about 24 time zones.
asks: Why is the time different in other countries?

facts: Earth turns once on its axis every 23 hours 56 minutes relative to the stars; a solar day is 24 hours.
At any moment, half of the Earth is lit by the Sun.
